findings.summary: The machine-readable scenario catalog contains oracle_state and expected_conformance_bounds beside the run scenario metadata, but no sanitized system-visible manifest or mandatory field-level separation is defined.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-18 passes the design catalog or a direct scenario_manifest_ref to a delegate, baseline, classifier, or verifier. The system can read expected occurrence, duplicate, or conformance outcomes before producing its result.
findings.consequence: This permits hidden-oracle leakage and circular conformance/scoring. It violates the declared CF-9/CF-3 boundary and can invalidate every comparative metric even if the implementation never reads a separate scorer oracle.
findings.recommended_disposition: Split public run manifests from scorer-only expected truth and require outcome-independent scenario identifiers and metadata.

findings.summary: ACCORD-02A result kinds VERIFIED, CORROBORATED, NO_EFFECT_OBSERVED, UNKNOWN_PENDING, and UNKNOWN_TERMINAL are not normatively mapped to the multidimensional ACCORD-02C/D settlement axes.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-02, ADV-11, and ADV-13 require the implementation to translate provider acceptance, task completion, or terminal unknown into C occurrence, stage, freshness, reopening, and finality fields.
findings.consequence: Different implementations can make different conclusions from the same A result wrapper, including silently treating VERIFIED as universal effect truth or NO_EFFECT_OBSERVED as profile-bounded non-occurrence.
findings.recommended_disposition: Add a machine-readable result-vocabulary map that preserves non-equivalence and requires predicate, profile, and axis semantics.

findings.summary: ACCORD-02B produces direct grant relations and effective-authority states, while ACCORD-02C/D also carry event-time authority validity statuses; D collapses relation/state values into one relation_or_state field.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-05, ADV-06, ADV-07, ADV-08, and ADV-15 supply ATTENUATED, CONTAINED, POSSIBLE_WIDENING, or UNKNOWN analysis while the combined result also asks for AUTHORIZED or INVALID_AUTHORITY.
findings.consequence: A future implementation could mistake grant attenuation or effective containment for a valid authorization decision, or mistake invalid authority for a widening relation. That undermines the authority/effect orthogonality claim at the machine-readable boundary.
findings.recommended_disposition: Separate direct relation, effective-authority composition, and event-time validity into typed fields with explicit source and evaluation time.

findings.summary: A/C use verifier_run_id and result_id, while D uses experiment run_id and result_record_id; D result_ref is an untyped string and does not require a schema-identified C result or verifier lineage.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-03 and ADV-16 produce valid-looking experimental records in which a result record, verifier result, provider operation, or experiment run can be confused during external reproduction.
findings.consequence: A third party may be unable to determine which verifier invocation emitted which settlement, or may correlate evidence to the wrong run without violating the D schema.
findings.recommended_disposition: Require typed references and a complete lineage from experiment run to D result_record_id to verifier_run_id and A/C result_id.

findings.summary: C requires predicate/stage-aware settlement, but A has no first-class logical effect/predicate record and D does not require predicate or stage on every attempt/evidence binding.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-04 and ADV-17 use a correct resource or reused effect_id with a different recipient or stage. ADV-11 supplies provider/task completion without a typed downstream predicate binding.
findings.consequence: The prose says early-stage evidence cannot settle a later stage, but underspecified portable records can require undocumented reconstruction or profile translation before that rule is machine-checkable.
findings.recommended_disposition: Require effect/predicate/stage references and explicit attempt/no-attempt binding on every settlement-relevant evidence path.

findings.summary: Baseline fairness and classifier restrictions are explicit in prose but not enforced by a per-arm input manifest or field-level allowlist; baseline output is open-ended and the catalog contains oracle-bearing metadata.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-19 supplies ARM-C an Accord-only evidence-class or settlement label while retaining a nominal ARM-C result record.
findings.consequence: The experiment could appear to compare ordinary engineering baselines while giving a baseline an Accord-specific feature, creating leakage or an unfair comparison without violating the current D schema.
findings.recommended_disposition: Freeze arm-specific visible inputs and artifact allowlists, and require the scorer to audit the actual input projection for every run.

findings.summary: Provider operation identifiers are correctly described as non-authoritative, but reuse/collision across logical effects has no explicit profile rule in the machine-readable linkage.
findings.adversarial_construction: ADV-10 and ADV-16 reuse or expire provider operation identifiers during retry and cross-effect cases.
findings.consequence: A careless implementation could use a provider operation ID as a uniqueness key even though the prose prohibits replacing effect_id or attempt_id.
findings.recommended_disposition: Add an explicit provider-operation reuse/collision policy and diagnostic requirement.

findings.summary: The first scored minimum requires local and MCP-shaped transports and two surfaces; A2A-shaped transport and the staged S3 surface are defined but not required in the core scored subset.
findings.adversarial_construction: A future result could be described broadly as transport-neutral or staged-effect coverage after exercising only the minimum subset.
findings.consequence: The claim scope could be overstated even though the minimum experimental design is compliant.
findings.recommended_disposition: Keep minimum and optional coverage labels explicit in future reports and do not generalize untested T3/S3 behaviour.

findings.summary: The stack preserves the prior-art boundary and does not claim novelty for delegated credentials, durable execution, receipts, idempotency, reconciliation, or related established mechanisms.
findings.adversarial_construction: Claim audit searched for novelty and empirical-result language presented as established fact.
findings.consequence: No defect found; future reports must still keep empirical conclusions conditional.

findings.summary: Conformance and empirical research are explicitly separated, and universal UNKNOWN is not treated as an automatic victory.
findings.adversarial_construction: Review tested whether deterministic vector success or universal abstention was described as a research win.
findings.consequence: No defect found; the distinction should remain prominent in acceptance materials.
